schema.length: {min_words, max_words} acceptable answer length for this question

schema.min_distinct_cited: minimum number of distinct [SN] sources the answer should cite

Zotero was faster (2 min 15 s)

questions.type: paraphrased (no keyword overlap), single document, Spanish question
questions.question: ¿Suelen los autores de revisiones sistemáticas indicar en sus artículos qué programa de gestión bibliográfica utilizaron? Compáralo con lo que ocurre con el software estadístico y explica la posible razón.
questions.minimum_answer: Most (79.5%) used a reference manager but only 4.8% reported it, versus 76.9% reporting their statistical software; likely cause: guidelines (ICMJE, PRISMA) do not ask for it. Answer must be in Spanish.

facts.text: 79.5% had used reference management software
only 4.8% reported it in the published review
76.9% reported their statistical software
reporting guidelines (ICMJE, PRISMA) do not mention reference software
source_patterns: ICMJE|International Committee of Medical Journal Editors

questions.judge_notes: The question avoids the words 'reference management software usage' / 'underreporting'; retrieval must work semantically. Credit the reason only if tied to missing reporting guidance, not to a speculation unsupported by the source.
questions.inference: Not stated as a fact: the authors only speculate that the discrepancy 'may be the result of an absence of guidelines'. A good answer presents this as the paper's tentative explanation (not as proven) and links it to ICMJE asking for statistical but not reference software, and PRISMA not requiring either.

questions.question: Do the sources in the library agree on how well Zotero handles importing PDFs and extracting their bibliographic metadata? Contrast what the different studies report.
questions.minimum_answer: Disagreement: Cai et al. found Zotero good at importing/indexing PDFs with accurate entries (and Mendeley failing to extract accurately), whereas Jin et al. state Zotero's PDF import requires manual metadata updates and its imports can be incomplete or inconsistent. Must attribute each view to its source and cite at least two documents.

facts.text: Cai et al.: Zotero is good at importing/indexing PDFs with accurate entries
source_patterns: better at importing and indexing PDF inputs

facts.text: Jin et al.: Zotero PDF import requires manual metadata updates / imports can be incomplete
source_patterns: PDF import requires manual metadata updates

facts.text: Mendeley often failed to extract accurate information from PDFs
source_patterns: Mendeley constantly failed to extract accurate information

facts.text: the answer explicitly says the sources point in different directions (inference: no source states the disagreement)

questions.judge_notes: Good answers state that the sources are not in full agreement, attribute each position to the right paper, and do not claim a consensus. Basak is only relevant for what Zotero imports from Google Scholar (it lacks DOI/URL), not for PDFs. Penalise an answer that merges the two views into one unattributed claim.
questions.inference: No source says the papers disagree. The answer must notice that Cai et al. (Zotero 'better at importing and indexing PDF inputs', accurate entries) and Jin et al. (Table 1: 'PDF import requires manual metadata updates'; metadata imports 'incomplete or inconsistent') point in opposite directions, attribute each view correctly, and may add the explanation that the studies differ in method (timed user study vs descriptive review) and date. Merging them into one consensus claim is wrong.

questions.type: multi-document reasoning, conceptual question with no verbatim phrase
questions.question: Why can Mendeley, but not Zotero, serve as a data source for readership-based indicators of scholarly impact, and what did validating such indicators against citation counts show?
questions.minimum_answer: Li et al.: RefWorks, EndNote and Zotero do not provide user-count data, so they cannot be used for research evaluation; Mendeley does, covers more articles than CiteULike, and its user counts correlate significantly with Web of Science citations (Spearman 0.559 Nature, 0.540 Science: 'high'). Chen et al.: Zotero never required registration and has no API to download data (so its users cannot be counted), while Mendeley's API exposes users' disciplines and academic status.

facts.text: Zotero/EndNote/RefWorks do not provide user-count data
source_patterns: RefWorks, EndNote and Zotero do not provide this data

facts.text: Zotero has no API / never required registration (Chen et al.)
source_patterns: Zotero does not provide an API

facts.text: Mendeley's API provides users' disciplines and academic status
Mendeley user counts correlate significantly/highly with citations
source_patterns: correlations between Mendeley user counts and WoS/Google Scholar citation counts are high

facts.text: concludes Zotero is unusable for readership indicators because its data is not accessible (no counts, no API, no registration), not because it is unpopular

questions.judge_notes: Needs two independent papers: Li et al. (user counts, correlations) and Chen et al. (Zotero API/registration, Mendeley API metadata). An answer using only one paper is capped at partial credit. Penalise claims that Zotero is unpopular or small - the sources say its users cannot be counted, not that there are few.
questions.inference: Chain: (1) Li et al.: reader counts are the indicator; RefWorks, EndNote and Zotero do not provide user-count data, so they cannot be used. (2) Chen et al.: Zotero never required registration and offers no API to download data, so its users cannot be counted; Mendeley's API exposes each article's readers' discipline and status. (3) Conclusion the answer must draw: Zotero is excluded because the data is not accessible, not because it is small or unpopular. (4) Li's validation: Mendeley user counts correlate highly with citations (Spearman about 0.54-0.56) but are a different, readership-type signal. Credit the (3) conclusion only if it is reached from (1)+(2).

questions.type: multi-document comparison, German question, technical RAG papers
questions.question: Vergleiche PyZoBot und HySemRAG: Wie machen beide Systeme ihre generierten Antworten überprüfbar, und welche Retrieval-Ansätze und Sprachmodelle setzen sie ein?
questions.minimum_answer: PyZoBot: Zotero library via Streamlit UI, standard RAG and knowledge-graph RAG, OpenAI (GPT-3.5-Turbo/GPT-4o) or open-source models (LLaMA 3.1, Mistral via Ollama); shows the document chunks used plus automatic citations/references. HySemRAG: hybrid retrieval (semantic search + keyword filtering + knowledge-graph traversal) on Qdrant vectors and a Neo4j graph; agentic self-correction and a post-hoc citation audit (99.0% citation accuracy in validated responses). Answer must be in German and cover both systems.

facts.text: both systems are discussed
PyZoBot displays the document chunks used and automatic citations
PyZoBot: OpenAI models or open-source LLaMA/Mistral via Ollama
PyZoBot offers standard and knowledge-graph RAG
HySemRAG: post-hoc citation verification (99.0% citation accuracy)
HySemRAG: hybrid retrieval (semantic + keyword + knowledge graph), Qdrant and Neo4j
contrasts user-side transparency (PyZoBot shows chunks + citations) with system-side automatic audit (HySemRAG post-hoc citation verification)

questions.judge_notes: Hardest item: two long preprints, German question, technical terms that stay English. Check each mechanism is attributed to the right system (the post-hoc citation audit and Neo4j/Qdrant belong to HySemRAG; Streamlit/Ollama/chunk display belong to PyZoBot). Mixing them up is a factual error.
questions.inference: Abstraction required: both systems pursue verifiability but differently. PyZoBot makes answers checkable by the human (shows the retrieved chunks with automatic citations/references); HySemRAG verifies automatically and systematically (agentic self-correction, then a post-hoc audit of every citation against the ground-truth database, 99.0% citation accuracy). The answer should draw this contrast (user-side transparency vs system-side audit) and keep the retrieval stacks apart (PyZoBot: standard or knowledge-graph RAG, OpenAI or LLaMA/Mistral via Ollama; HySemRAG: hybrid semantic+keyword+knowledge-graph retrieval over Qdrant and Neo4j).
